task_instance: Attempted to pull new docket entries for a sample federal case (e.g., case no. 1:24-cv-01234, N.D. Ill.) from PACER since a given last-update date, and produce docket_update.md summarizing each new filing (filer, relief sought, deadlines) with new deadlines listed at top.
blocker_detail: Step 1 of the skill requires logging in to PACER with the firm's PACER account (username/password) to open the docket report for the case, and PACER is a paid, credentialed, account-bound federal court service (also charges per-page fees for docket downloads). The office-assistant runtime and safety rules explicitly forbid using or searching for credentials/tokens and forbid account-bound or paid services. Without authenticated PACER access, the docket report and filed documents for any specific case cannot be retrieved at all -- public web search/fetch does not expose PACER's per-case, authenticated docket data (CM/ECF), so there is no way to obtain the actual list of new filings for a real case number. This blocks the task at the very first step, before any summarization or file-writing work could occur.
evidence: Read SKILL.md, which specifies 'Log in to PACER with the firm's account'. Confirmed via general knowledge and a web search that PACER (Public Access to Court Electronic Records) requires an individual/firm account with login credentials and charges $0.10/page for most documents/reports, and has no public, unauthenticated API or page that returns a given case's docket sheet. Per the runtime's safety rules (no credentials/tokens, no account-bound or paid services), this cannot be attempted, so the task stops at step 1. No docket_update.md could be produced because there is no real docket data obtainable without violating the credential/paid-service restriction.
